title: The filter chrome exposes accessible controls and refetches every tile with the same boundary
asA: operator narrowing the dashboard with a filter chip or a filter input
iWant: the filter chrome to expose accessible controls that carry the operator's choice to every fetch and refetch every tile with the same boundary
soThat: the shell renders a filtered view at one boundary without drifting between tiles

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard surface with filter chrome, every filter control (chip, dropdown, search input) is a labelled interactive element (a `<button>`, a `<select>` or an `<input>`) with an accessible name; the controls are keyboard-reachable in reading order before the tile row; the operator's active filter selection is reflected on the shell as a `data-active-filters` attribute the pack can read. A filter chrome that ships hover-only controls (a hover-reveal menu on a mouseover element) fails project-side check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard with filter chrome
acceptanceCriteria.then: every filter control is a labelled interactive element keyboard-reachable in reading order

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an operator-driven filter change (activate a filter chip, type into a filter input), the shell issues one refetch per tile and one per rendered chart with the same `filter` query parameter set applied to every fetch; the shell's `data-active-filters` attribute updates on the same paint as the refetch batch. This AC is a runtime-observable fan-out clause; the pack asserts the fetch fan-out on the timeframe seam (AC-19104-1) which the fixture drives; the filter fan-out is a mechanism-reach gap the README names for a v1.1 minor bump.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard and a filter change
acceptanceCriteria.then: every refetch carries the same active-filters set and the shell attribute updates

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard with a filter input, when the operator types a value that violates the input's `pattern` or exceeds its `maxlength`, the shell does NOT fire a refetch; the filter chrome surfaces an accessible inline validation message (`aria-describedby` on the input pointing at the message region) and the tile grid retains its last successful state.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator typing an invalid value into a filter input (pattern/maxlength violation)
acceptanceCriteria.then: no refetch fires, an accessible inline validation message announces the failure, and the tile grid retains its last successful state

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a filter change that fires a fan-out refetch and a subset of tile fetches reject (2 of 6 return 5xx or time out), the shared `as of <ISO-8601>` stamp advances after every tile has SETTLED (succeeded or failed) and the failed tiles enter the error state with the shared stamp; a shell whose stamp advances only after successful tiles fails the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a filter change fan-out where a subset of tile fetches reject
acceptanceCriteria.then: the shared as-of stamp advances after every tile has settled and the failed tiles are in the error state carrying the shared stamp

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a filter reset action (a `Clear filters` control on the chrome), when the operator activates it, every filter control reverts to its default value, one refetch fires per tile and per chart with no filter parameters, and the tile grid re-renders on the response; the reset action is keyboard-reachable and carries an accessible name matching `Clear filters` or an equivalent.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator activating the Clear filters control
acceptanceCriteria.then: every filter control reverts to default, one refetch fires per tile and per chart without filter parameters, and the reset control is keyboard-reachable with an accessible name
